name: embedded-template-anchor
body:
Anchoring consideration: the tier-4 content change is to agent markdown templates embedded into the binary via `include_str!` (the SUITE_TOOLS/AGENTS constants in src/main.rs). The anchor is chosen for DELIVERY semantics, not because markdown is unscannable: the distributed agent prompts are embedded constants delivered to the user-level suite by `apg.install_suite` (the `apg` entrypoint `apg.main`, plus `apg.cmd_init` / `apg.install_suite` — src/main.rs), so the durable delivered artifact is the embedded text plus its install path, and the `implemented-by` spine anchors there rather than on a repo-tree `.md` file.

Markdown is a scanned language under `requirements.requirement.markdown-frontend`: once .md/.markdown are accepted, `opencode-suite/agents/*.md` and AGENTS.md enter the graph as File nodes (FQN = the absolute path) with Struct section nodes, and a scanned .md File FQN is a LEGITIMATE `implemented-by` target — the code-FQN universe is Module/Struct/Function/File records with no `status` set (src/main.rs:1342-1364), and `classify_code_ref` grades Real/Pending/Drift off that universe (src/layers.rs:1295-1329), independent of file extension. See `solution.note.markdown-anchoring`.

The plan-writer must express "edit these embedded templates" (the `opencode-suite/**` source-of-truth + its worktree mirror) as the tier-4 delta, and keeps the anchor on the embedding/install Rust because that is the delivered artifact — a deliberate delivery-semantics choice, not a claim that a `.md` path will not resolve.
